title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft section (the page has many strike-outs) of the notes for the 1976 IHES talk on the divided-power de Rham complex. It belongs to a technical chapter on the Dold–Puppe (Dold–Kan) correspondence 'DP' between complexes and (co)simplicial objects, for a k-linear (Karoubian) category B, its presheaf category B^ and enriched Hom's. Hom^*_k is the Hom of cosimplicial or simplicial objects with values in modules, defined in 'prop. 3'.

(1) Top of page. A functor F on B (extended to B^) is expressed through a universal cosimplicial object C^*_F := F(C^*):
 F(x) ≃ Hom^*_k(α^*(x), C^*_F).
Here α^* is presumably the adjoint 'cosimplicial realization' of x, and C^* = (C^n) is the standard cosimplicial object.

(2) Struck-out first attempt. Grothendieck pairs F(x) ⊗ α^{[n]}(x) → C^{[n]}_F, using Hom(x, C^{[n]}) on one side and F(C^{[n]}) on the other. He plans to:
- define the comparison map as in prop. 3, inside B^;
- prove it is an isomorphism by reducing to representables of the form C^i_k, by Kan extension or density.
The replacement margin text says the isomorphism follows formally from the definitions of α^*, the adjunction, and the description of C_F through DP.

(3) Main argument. Take K· a complex of k-modules, C· a complex in B, K^* = DP(K·) and C^* = DP(C·). Then DP induces a canonical isomorphism, functorial in B^:
 Hom_k(K·, C·) ≃ Hom^*_k(K^*, C^*).
This is the enriched full faithfulness of the Dold–Kan equivalence. The page then concludes by prop. 3.

(4) Struck-out draft of Prop 6, finalised on the previous page. The normalized chain functor ND from simplicial k-modules to chain complexes is co-represented by a cosimplicial family of simplicial modules:
 ND(L_*)_i ≃ Hom_{k,*}(C^i_*, L_*), with C^i_* identified with the exterior power Λ^i𝔏_*.
The boundary map ND_i → ND_{i-1} is the transpose of the coboundary C^{i-1}_* → C^i_*.
The next page supplies the input: 𝔏_* = (I ↦ k^I) is contractible, 𝔏/k is a K(k,1), and Λ^i(𝔏/k) is a K(k,i).
So the co-representing objects of the normalized complex are exterior powers of the simplicial model of K(k,1). This is a Koszul / de Rham–type description, presumably preparing the divided-power de Rham complex of a simplicial ring.
errors: The transcription line 'C^* = DP(K·)' must be C^* = DP(C·) for the statement to make sense; this is probably a transcription slip.
Prop 6 on this page is struck out and only sketched: the compatibility of differentials is left as 'petites vérifications' on the previous page. No genuine mathematical error is visible.

ideas.what: Enriched full faithfulness of the Dold–Puppe correspondence: Hom of complexes ≃ Hom of associated (co)simplicial objects, functorial in the presheaf category
ideas.where_published: Used implicitly via Illusie, Complexe cotangent (1971); Grothendieck's own texts unsure

ideas.what: Representing a functor F by a universal cosimplicial object C^*_F = F(C^*), with F(x) ≃ Hom^*(α^*(x), C^*_F), proved by reduction to representables / Kan extension
ideas.modern_name: Density / Yoneda–Kan extension along the standard cosimplicial object (nerve–realization adjunction)

ideas.what: Normalized chain functor co-represented by the cosimplicial simplicial modules Λ^i𝔏_* (with 𝔏 = k^I), the differential being the transpose of coboundaries
ideas.modern_name: Co-representability of normalized chains by k[Δ^i]/k[∂Δ^i] ≃ K(k,i) models; Λ^i(K(k,1)) ≃ K(k,i) (décalage)

deep.surprise_reason: Draft-level technical page establishing standard Dold–Kan and representability facts as tools for the divided-power de Rham complex. The exterior-power model of the co-representing objects is a nice touch, but it follows from well-known décalage facts and is not new.
transcription_corrections: 'K^· ∈ M_k' is probably 'K^· ∈ Ab_k' (or the category of complexes of k-modules).
In the struck Prop 6, the object written under C^i_* is Λ^i𝔏_* (exterior power of the simplicial module 𝔏), consistent with the previous page.
The top-left margin reads approximately 'cela fournit un iso de foncteurs ... sur B^ ... Kan-...', i.e. a Kan-extension remark; the precise wording is uncertain.
